items.title: Determining the Maximum and Minimum Values of a Vertically Stretched Sine or Cosine Function

sections.normalized_html: What is the minimum value of [MATH: y=2\sin x?]
sections.readable_text: What is the minimum value of [MATH: y=2\sin x?]

sections.normalized_html: EXPLANATION
sections.readable_text: EXPLANATION

sections.normalized_html:
Method 1

To plot the given curve, we follow these steps:

  • Start with the graph of [MATH: y=\sin x.]

  • Then, stretch it parallel to the [MATH: y]-axis by a stretch factor of [MATH: 2.]

The resulting graph is shown below.

From the graph, we see that the minimum value is [MATH: y=-2]

Method 2

We know that that [MATH: y = \sin{x}] has a minimum value of [MATH: -1.]

[MATH: \sin{x} \geq -1]

Multiplying both sides of the above inequality by [MATH: 2] gives:

[MATH: 2 ⋅ \sin x|≥ 2 ⋅ (− 1); 2\sin x|≥ − 2]

Therefore, the minimum value of [MATH: 2\sin{x}] is [MATH: -2.]

items.readable_text:
Content:
The amplitude of a sine function or cosine function represents half the distance between the maximum and minimum values of the function.

Graphic:
[IMG: /graphics/4d787c7d56cfa4b65d4038768fee1aa4]

Content:
We can calculate the amplitude using the minimum and maximum values [MATH: y_\min] and [MATH: y_\max\mathbin{:}]
[MATH: \textrm{Amplitude } =\dfrac{y_\max - y_\min}2]

Content:
For example, the amplitude of the function [MATH: y=\sin x] shown above, where [MATH: y_\min =-1] and [MATH: y_\max =1], is

Content:
[MATH: Amplitude|= (1 − (− 1))/(2); = (1 + 1)/(2); = (2)/(2); = 1.]

sections.normalized_html: What is the amplitude of [MATH: f(x)=2\cos{x}?]
sections.readable_text: What is the amplitude of [MATH: f(x)=2\cos{x}?]

sections.normalized_html: EXPLANATION
sections.readable_text: EXPLANATION

sections.normalized_html:
To plot the given curve, we follow these steps:

  • Start with the graph of [MATH: y=\cos x.]

  • Then, stretch it parallel to the [MATH: y]-axis by a stretch factor of [MATH: 2.]

The resulting graph is shown below.

From the graph, we see that the maximum value is [MATH: y_\max=2] and the minimum value is [MATH: y_\min=-2.] Therefore, the amplitude is

[MATH: Amplitude|= (y_{max} − y_{min})/(2); = (2 − (− 2))/(2); = (2 + 2)/(2); = (4)/(2); = 2.]

Item 6 — Example: Determining the Maximum and Minimum Values of a Vertically Stretched Sine or Cosine Function

Example Prompt:
What is the minimum value of [MATH: y=2\sin x?]

Content:
EXPLANATION

Explanation:
Method 1

To plot the given curve, we follow these steps:

- Start with the graph of [MATH: y=\sin x.]
- Then, stretch it parallel to the [MATH: y]-axis by a stretch factor of [MATH: 2.]

The resulting graph is shown below.

[IMG: /graphics/376ef1e1c1b18ebc1970e8019692e0f8]

From the graph, we see that the minimum value is [MATH: y=-2]

Method 2

We know that that [MATH: y = \sin{x}] has a minimum value of [MATH: -1.]

[MATH: \sin{x} \geq -1]

Multiplying both sides of the above inequality by [MATH: 2] gives:

[MATH: 2 ⋅ \sin x|≥ 2 ⋅ (− 1); 2\sin x|≥ − 2]

Therefore, the minimum value of [MATH: 2\sin{x}] is [MATH: -2.]

Item 9 — Tutorial: The Amplitude of Trigonometric Functions

Content:
The amplitude of a sine function or cosine function represents half the distance between the maximum and minimum values of the function.

Graphic:
[IMG: /graphics/4d787c7d56cfa4b65d4038768fee1aa4]

Content:
We can calculate the amplitude using the minimum and maximum values [MATH: y_\min] and [MATH: y_\max\mathbin{:}]
[MATH: \textrm{Amplitude } =\dfrac{y_\max - y_\min}2]

Content:
For example, the amplitude of the function [MATH: y=\sin x] shown above, where [MATH: y_\min =-1] and [MATH: y_\max =1], is

Content:
[MATH: Amplitude|= (1 − (− 1))/(2); = (1 + 1)/(2); = (2)/(2); = 1.]

Item 10 — Example: Determining the Amplitude Given the Equation of a Vertically Stretched Sine or Cosine Function

Example Prompt:
What is the amplitude of [MATH: f(x)=2\cos{x}?]

Content:
EXPLANATION

Explanation:
To plot the given curve, we follow these steps:

- Start with the graph of [MATH: y=\cos x.]
- Then, stretch it parallel to the [MATH: y]-axis by a stretch factor of [MATH: 2.]

The resulting graph is shown below.

[IMG: /graphics/7e4eba4e3e4fb7907c44977b4a96d51f]

From the graph, we see that the maximum value is [MATH: y_\max=2] and the minimum value is [MATH: y_\min=-2.] Therefore, the amplitude is

[MATH: Amplitude|= (y_{max} − y_{min})/(2); = (2 − (− 2))/(2); = (2 + 2)/(2); = (4)/(2); = 2.]
